Messages.Author: Jon Stahler
Messages.Body:
Ok...lets say I have Zoning Board in play.

During my untap, I name my prey's hunting ground. One of my minions plays
Kine Dominance at superior to steal the location and is successful. I now
control the hunting ground. Another of my minions now tries to take the
action to put the location away...

My questions are:

1. Can I still take the action even though the controller has changed? I
didn't notice anything in the cardtext that would indicate that the action
cannot still be taken.

2. Who gets the pool cost for the location? The controller or owner?

3. It goes into its OWNERS library, right? Not the controller? Cardtext
says owner, I believe (at work...don't have it in front of me) so I just
wanted to be sure.

4. The card says ANY minion...not any minion I control. Is this effect
similar to that of the Madness Network and lasts until the end of my minion
phase? In other words, when I'm done with my actions, can any other
untapped minion at the table tap to attempt this action? Or is the card
supposed to read any minion *you* control?

Sorry for not posting card text. I'm at work and the card is at home and
I've yet to see the text posted. Perhaps I'll throw it online when I go
home for lunch. Apologies if some of these are answered by card text.

Owner.

Messages.Author: The Bard of Crete
Messages.Body:
> I don't understand. Can you make D actions directed on something you
control?

No, if you take a D action at yourself, it becomes undirected.

>So, you would destroy the thing even though it is now yours, and gain
>pool, right ?

If I'm understanding everything correctly, yes. You destroy the location
you control and gain the pool. Doesn't matter who the owner is, the
controller is important.

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
The Bard of Crete wrote:
>
> > I don't understand. Can you make D actions directed on something you
> control?
>
> No, if you take a D action at yourself, it becomes undirected.

Correct. Actually, if you take an action at yourself it is undirected.
It was never D, so it doesn't "change" to undirected - it simply
is undirected. See section 6.2.2 of the rulebook.

> >So, you would destroy the thing even though it is now yours, and gain
> >pool, right ?
>
> If I'm understanding everything correctly, yes. You destroy the location
> you control and gain the pool. Doesn't matter who the owner is, the
> controller is important.

Correct.
